articles.title: Democrats Take Control of US Congress As Voters Reject Trump's Republicans
articles.content: Tuesday, November 3, was Election Day in the United States, and the results are (mostly) in: Democrats are projected to win control of both the House and Senate in the 2026 midterms. The blue wave turned out to be more of a blue tsunami, ending Republican control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump's second term. Democrats flipped seven Republican-held Senate seats in the 2026 midterms, including surprise victories in traditionally Republican strongholds such as Texas, Kansas, and South Carolina. Kansas elected its first Democratic U.S. senator in nearly 100 years (94 years to be exact), while Texas and South Carolina sent Democrats to the Senate for the first time in decades. Democrats also picked up seats in Ohio, Iowa, Maine, and North Carolina. Developing... Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: China outlines plans for moonshot it hopes to land by 2030
articles.content: China’s crewed space program has outlined plans for a moon landing it hopes to achieve by the year 2030. Deputy chief designer Wang Xiang explained the plans last weekend at an event called the Seventh Manned Space Symposium. Chinese state media has posted video of Wang discussing plans to reach Luna by launching two Long March 10 rockets. One will carry a lander named “Lanyue” and the other will hoist a crew capsule called “Mengzhou.” The two craft will meet in orbit around the Moon, where two of the three Taikonauts aboard Mengzhou will transfer to Lanyue and descend to set boot on regolith. In the video, Wang said China plans near-Earth orbit test missions for both vehicles in coming years, followed by an uncrewed visit to the Moon. If all goes well, China hopes to attempt a crewed landing by 2030. The Seventh Manned Space Symposium marked the 70th anniversary of the founding of China's space program and was also pitched as a moment for articulation of the nation’s ambitions in space under its 15 th five-year-plan, Beijing’s blueprint for the years 2026 to 2030. China called off its last moonshot in August, when authorities decided the Chang’e 7 robotic ice hunting mission “ failed to meet launch criteria ” just one day before its planned launch. The orbit required to reach the South Lunar Pole for that mission isn’t always easily accessible, so China plans to try again next year. When China tries to get Chang’e 7, Lanyue, and Mengzhou flying, it will at least have some new standards to apply to their operations after the China Manned Space Engineering Office last week published seventeen of them. One of the standards defines the architecture for Ethernet and Wi-Fi networks on China’s space station and other orbiters. Another governs signage used in orbit, in the hope that a standard means Taikonauts won’t make mistakes. A couple outline procedures for extravehicular activities, and use of a robotic arm to assist Taikonauts on such missions. Others explain the materials designers can choose from when building spacecraft. ®

articles.title: Texas wanted to power America’s AI boom. Its new governor could change everything
articles.content: Less than a year ago, Texas Governor Greg Abbott stood beside Sundar Pichai, the Google CEO, to celebrate the company’s $40 billion investment in the state’s cloud and AI infrastructure. Three new data center campuses would help make Texas, Abbott declared, the “ epicenter of AI development .” On Tuesday, Abbott, a Republican, lost his reelection bid to Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat who campaigned on halting new data center development until state lawmakers pass stronger protections for residents. At a press conference over the summer , Hinojosa accused corporations of taking advantage of Texans and operating with little oversight, blaming Abbott for creating the “Wild West of data centers.” Her stunning victory makes her the first Democrat elected governor of Texas since Ann Richards in 1990. And given that Texas is home to the country’s second-largest data center market , behind Virginia, the political upheaval could have profound implications for the artificial intelligence boom. The scale of Texas’s AI bet Texas’s $2.9 trillion economy is the nation’s second largest; if it were a country, it would rank eighth worldwide. It boasts abundant energy resources, a ton of relatively inexpensive land, and a historically light regulatory touch—all of which have enticed AI companies (and companies in seemingly every other sector , for that matter). Researchers at Rice University’s Baker Institute estimate that annual data center investment in Texas rose from $3.4 billion in 2022 to a projected $66.2 billion in 2026. And much more is in the pipeline. Texas accounts for roughly 26% of planned American data center capacity—nearly three times the amount planned in Virginia—according to an analysis by the investment bank Jefferies, as reported by The Wall Street Journal . Jefferies estimated that Hinojosa’s proposed moratorium could put 13.3 gigawatts of announced Texas data center projects at risk, potentially delaying construction or forcing developers to abandon their plans. Little wonder that Bank of America called the Texas governor’s race the most consequential contest of the 2026 midterms for utility and power markets. The stakes extend well beyond Texas. The companies racing to develop AI depend on enormous infrastructure investments that take years to plan and require far more than financing. They need electricity, water, land, permits—and, increasingly, the support of the communities where they hope to build. Who gets the benefits? And who pays the costs? Hinojosa has proposed a moratorium until lawmakers enact lasting safeguards. She also wants to prohibit nondisclosure agreements that keep communities in the dark, give residents greater say over new developments, and require companies to prove their projects won’t raise household water or electricity bills. And she wants to eliminate the government subsidies that have helped make Texas so attractive to developers. One of those subsidies is particularly lucrative. Qualifying data centers can avoid Texas’s 6.25% sales tax on equipment and other purchases for up to 20 years. The state comptroller projected that the exemption would cost $3.2 billion in foregone revenue over two years, potentially an underestimate. The industry argues the incentives attract investment, jobs, and other tax revenue. Critics question the public return when facilities can also place substantial demands on utilities and natural resources. The advantages didn’t end with tax breaks. A Texas Tribune analysis found that about half of planned data centers are slated for unincorporated areas, where counties generally lack the zoning authority cities use to regulate development. That can leave nearby residents with little say over projects that could transform their communities. And the scale of Texas’s AI ambitions is putting growing pressure on its resources. articles.title: Tencent WeVisOne-VL Unifies Detection, OCR, Segmentation and Matting
articles.content: Tencent’s WeChat Vision team has released WeVisOne-VL , an open vision language model in 2B and 4B sizes. The WeVisOne-VL vision language model handles detection, referring, counting, pointing, OCR, segmentation and alpha matting in one model. Pixel outputs come from a 9.6M-parameter decoder, so no separate SAM is needed. It also answers “None” when a queried object is absent. For developers, that can replace a detector, an OCR engine and a segmenter with one model. TL;DR Size: 2B ( 2.44B params ) and 4B ( 4.83B params ) on Hugging Face, and a 9.6M-parameter pixel decoder. Trained with up to 8,192 tokens of context; deployment context length is not disclosed. Runs on: A single GPU through Transformers or vLLM in BF16. The package also lists NPU and CPU devices. VRAM needs are not disclosed. A community GGUF ran object-level tasks on a 6 GB RTX 2060. Performance: Beats the same-scale VLM baselines in Tencent’s tables on most of 30+ benchmarks (self-reported). Best: 71.3 F1 Mean on Dense200 dense detection, versus 58.7 for LocateAnything-3B. Worst: 52.6% rejection rate on PR-Bench, so many absent-target queries still get a box. What is WeVisOne-VL? WeVisOne-VL (“WeChat Vision All-in-One”) is a perception-focused model from Tencent built on Qwen3-VL . It targets fine-grained localization rather than open-ended chat. Users choose the output granularity: points, boxes, binary masks or continuous alpha mattes. How does WeVisOne-VL work? Every task is cast as structured next-token prediction. The model adds coordinate tokens <0> to <1000> for normalized boxes and points. An absent target produces None instead of a guessed box. For pixel tasks, the model emits an <OBJ> token after each predicted box. Its hidden state becomes a query for the pixel decoder, according to the model card . The decoder has 3 parts: Visual Feature Adapter: reuses multi-level Qwen3-VL ViT features instead of a second image encoder. Box-Guided Query Decoder: 6 deformable cross-attention blocks seeded by the <OBJ> state and the box. Dense Prediction Head: refines output at S/4, S/2 and S/1 into a full-resolution mask or matte. How was it trained? A knowledge-graph-driven data engine annotated over 100M images with about 3.6B boxes. SAM3, Rex-Omni and an in-house detector proposed regions, and Qwen3-VL verified them. Training used 3 SFT stages. Stage 1 aligned output formats on 90M examples. Stage 2 raised input to 1,960 visual tokens and up to 500 boxes per response. Stage 3 trained the pixel decoder, then specialized it for matting on 130M samples. A final GRPO stage used 178K uncertainty-filtered examples, as described in the research paper . How does WeVisOne-VL perform on benchmarks? All numbers below are self-reported, using greedy decoding and at most 1,960 visual tokens per image. Detection, referring and OCR use F1 averaged over IoU 0.5 to 0.95. Detection: 55.3 F1 on LVIS and 71.3 on Dense200 for the 4B model. Referring: 81.8 F1 on RefCOCOg test, versus 77.6 for LocateAnything-3B. Rejection: 96.4% on Tencent’s in-house WeRef-Bench (2,880 queries), versus 73.0%. Counting: 89.6% exact-match on PixMo-Count test, versus 82.8%. OCR: 52.0 F1 on TotalText, ahead of the PP-OCRv5 specialist at 25.7. Segmentation: 71.2 gIoU on ReasonSeg val, versus 65.0 for LISA-13B. Matting: 7.3 MAD on P3M-500-NP box prompts, versus 15.4 for SAM2-Matting (SAM3). Lower is better. The 2B model trails the 4B model on most tasks. It still scores better box-prompted matting on P3M-500-NP, at 6.6 MAD. articles.title: AMD on track to overtake Intel as biggest x86 outfit
articles.content: AMD has predicted it will win more revenue than Intel in its next quarter, potentially marking the first time it becomes the dominant vendor whose main product is x86 processors. The house of Zen on Tuesday announced its Q3 2026 results, which saw it grow revenue 45 percent year-over-year to $13.4 billion. The company’s Data Center segment won $8.5 billion of revenue, up 97 percent year-over-year. Sales of silicon in AMD’s client and gaming segment slid eight percent to $3.7 billion, a worse fall than the five percent fall that helped to sink Intel’s share price . Intel, AMD’s great rival in the x86 market, offered revenue guidance of $15 billion to $16 billion for its next quarter, which would represent almost no growth. AMD, by contrast, told investors it expects around $17 billion of revenue next quarter. CEO Lisa Su predicted even better days are ahead. “We think 2027 is going to be a very strong momentum year for both the CPU business as well as the data center AI business,” she said on the company’s earnings call. “We have said the overall company will grow greater than 80 percent, and for the data center CPU business, we will about double, and for the data center AI business, it will significantly more than double.” Su said AMD is confident its supply chain can meet that demand. “We have worked across our supply chain to secure the wafers, substrates, advanced packaging, memory, and other key components needed to support much higher growth next year,” she said. “We are also deepening our collaboration with our supply chain partners and investing alongside them to secure the long-term capacity our growth will require.” The CEO added that AMD has “strong confidence in our ability to sustain exceptional revenue growth for years to come, with earnings growing even faster.” If those predictions are correct, AMD will likely accelerate away from Intel to become the leading provider of x86 processors after years of challenging Chipzilla's lead. Intel would still have higher overall revenue, due to its foundry operations, but in terms of revenue earned from selling chips, AMD would become the market leader. AMD is arguably already the server CPU technology leader, and while it is second to Nvidia in the GPU market has trounced Intel. Even AMD's declining client and gaming revenue has an upside because it was the gaming part of the portfolio that created the problem. PC chip sales rose seven percent year-over-year to $2.9 billion. Su said strong sales of Ryzen mobile processors drove that growth. “Commercial is becoming a larger part of our client business as large enterprises adopt Ryzen PRO PCs across their employee base,” she said, pointing to strong adoption at the world’s largest banks, automotive companies, and healthcare concerns. Big corporate buyers are often a source of bigger profits and/or steadier revenue, so AMD looks to be taking the cream off the top of the PC market rather than scrounging for SMB and retail scraps. Investors liked what they heard, sending AMD’s share price up by around five percent in after hours trading. ®

articles.title: iPad Mini review: A pricey delight
articles.content: For a device with such a straightforward name, the iPad Mini has had many lives over its 14 years. Yes, it’s always been a small iPad. But at various times, it’s also been a cheap iPad with a lesser display, an iPad as technologically sophisticated as any you could buy, and a midrange iPad. Last week, Apple announced a new iPad—one of the remarkably large number of products the company introduced during what may have been its most productive October ever. It remains a small iPad. But the new version replaces the LCD screen of past versions with OLED, a technology previously available only in the iPad Pro. That’s one of several upgrades that take the new Mini to a tier of its own—not quite on the level of the iPad Pro, but in some respects above the iPad Air models the previous Mini closely resembled. The new iPad Mini also costs $100 more than its predecessor. That version went up $100 itself in June, when Apple raised many of its prices in reaction to the AI-induced RAM shortage . Now the Mini starts at an imposing $699 for the Wi-Fi version with 128 GB of storage, a 40% increase in a little over four months, and just $50 less than the cheapest iPad Air. (The basic, entry-level iPad also went up $100, but I still consider it a bargain at $449.) Even if the iPad Mini is no longer an impulse item for most of us, it remains the present-day iPad that reminds me most of Steve Jobs’s keynote introduction of the original 2010 iPad . In it, he outlined the need for the device and did much of his demo from the comfort of a cushy chair. That niche—bigger than a phone, more intimate than a laptop—is alive, well, and still evolving in the new Mini. [Photo: Apple] The Mini’s roomy screen lets it do many things well that an iPhone can’t, unless it’s an iPhone Duo . Unlike its larger iPad siblings, however, it’s not trying to encroach on the traditional territory of a MacBook or other PCs. It’s a tablet in the category’s purest sense. (I am aware that third-party manufacturers have long made keyboard cases for iPad Minis and will surely offer ones for this model—I just can’t envision even that setup replacing anyone’s laptop.) Since the beginning, the Mini has been all about size, weight, and the pleasure of spending time with a device that you can hold for extended periods—in one hand, even—without it seeming to grow mysteriously heavier over time. It’s also been the easiest iPad to grab and take almost anywhere, maybe in a jacket pocket. After all these years, Apple is still finding ways to wring heft out of the new Mini’s design. Compared to the previous version, the most striking improvements are the 16% reduction in thickness and (for the Wi-Fi model) 13.8% reduction in weight. But Apple also shrank the display’s border by 25%, which allowed it to increase the screen size from 8.3 inches to 8.5 inches, even though the new model is slightly narrower. It’s about 45% lighter than the 11-inch iPad Air and 59% lighter than the 13-inch Air. Consequently, this tablet is a delight for tasks where more display real estate than a (non-folding) phone is desirable, but 11 or 13 inches may be overkill—long-form reading on the web or in an e-reader app, gaming, viewing and wrangling photos, lightweight productivity such as email triage. It’s also an extremely pleasant way to watch video, assuming you’re not trying to re-create the experience of watching a blockbuster movie in the theater. And its support for Apple Pencil Pro makes it a beguiling digital sketchbook when you’re out and about and lugging a larger iPad would feel like a burden. As for the new OLED screen, it delivers on the technology’s promise by providing deep blacks, rich colors, and peak brightness of 1,200 nits, compared to 500 nits for the previous model. Some people— such as Multicore ’s Sam Byford —regret that the display doesn’t include Apple’s ProMotion technology, which uses a variable refresh rate to make scrolling and input smoother and more responsive. articles.title: How to handle a water spill on your Mac before the damage gets worse
articles.content: A liquid spill can damage your Mac long after the surface dries, making a quick response essential to avoiding an expensive repair. Here's how to limit the damage and give your Mac the best chance of recovery. If you spill water on your Mac If you spill water on your Mac, shut it down, disconnect power, and blot away visible moisture before checking how far the liquid spread. Water can seep through the keyboard, ports, and gaps in the enclosure, reaching sensitive components even when the outside looks dry. A few drops on the aluminum enclosure are different from a full cup of coffee spilling across the keyboard. The amount of liquid, where it enters, and what it contains all affect the risk of damage. Coffee, soda, and other drinks can also leave behind residue that causes problems long after the liquid evaporates. Liquid damage isn't always obvious, and a Mac that continues working after a spill isn't necessarily safe to use. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

articles.title: Journify Raises $12M Series A Amid 5x Growth
articles.content: Investors back Journify’s push into the US and Europe Journify , the ad signal infrastructure company, today announced a $12 million Series A at four times its previous valuation. Al Mada Ventures led the round, co-led by returning investor Silicon Badia, with Shorooq and Bunat Ventures increasing their investment and Du Ventures and Oraseya Capital joining as new investors. The funding will take Journify into the US and Europe and expand the AI behind its platform. Global ad spend will exceed $1 trillion in 2026, with algorithms expected to place three quarters by 2028, according to dentsu. These systems learn from the customer outcomes brands send back. Browser restrictions, broken tracking, and disconnected offline sales leave them with an incomplete picture of who buys. Journify makes sure ad platforms such as Google, Meta, TikTok, Snap and Amazon Ads see the purchases, sign-ups and store sales a brand’s customers actually make. More than 100 businesses use Journify today, from fast-growing ecommerce brands to some of the region’s largest retailers, representing hundreds of millions of dollars in annual ad spend. Customers include Jarir Bookstore, one of Saudi Arabia’s largest retailers, which increased its return on ad spend on Meta by 182%, and Saudi ecommerce brand Baytonia, which grew its return on ad spend on TikTok by 80% while cutting cost per purchase by 44%. “AI is transforming advertising, but the intelligence behind it is only as good as the signals it receives,” said Taoufik El Jamali, Co-Founder and CEO of Journify. “Businesses know who buys, who comes back and what creates lasting customer value. Too little of that knowledge reaches the ad platforms driving their growth. Our vision is to close that gap, turning real customer outcomes into intelligence ad platforms can learn from. We’re building toward a future where advertising AI understands what makes a customer valuable to each business, not just what makes them click.”“As AI takes on a greater role in marketing, we believe the connection between reliable customer data and the decisions built on it will become increasingly valuable,” said Omar Laalej, Managing Director at Al Mada Ventures. “What interests us about Journify is its approach to building that connection from the data layer up: a privacy-first foundation that can evolve into intelligence and action. The founders’ understanding of that opportunity gives us confidence in their ability to build a platform that marketers can increasingly rely on, both to understand their customers and to act on that understanding.”Hossam Shafick, Partner at Silicon Badia, Seed Lead and returning investor, added, “Since our initial investment, Journify has grown its valuation by more than 4x, and its revenues more than 5x, validating both the strength of its technology and the team’s ability to execute at scale. That performance has deepened our conviction that Journify can become a global leader in ad signal infrastructure. We are proud to double down and co-lead this round as the company expands into the world’s largest advertising markets.” Journify already uses AI to monitor every connection continuously, detect signal-quality issues and fix them. The new funding will grow those capabilities as Journify expands beyond the GCC. In the US alone, digital advertising revenue reached $294.6 billion in 2025, according to IAB and PwC. “I’m excited to help Journify scale in the biggest ad market in the world,” said Ryan Burke, a newly appointed member of Journify’s board and three-time Chief Revenue Officer. “I’ve known Taoufik since our InVision days, and I’ve seen his product execution in action. Based on the success they’re already seeing in the Middle East, it’s not a question whether it works in the US, but how fast we can scale.” About Journify Journify builds ad signal infrastructure for performance marketers. articles.title: Filing: Amazon’s previously announced layoffs include 95 jobs in Washington state
articles.content: Most of the employees in the latest Washington notice are based in Amazon’s Seattle offices. (GeekWire File Photo) A notice made public Tuesday evening, disclosing about 95 Amazon job cuts in Washington state, is part of the company’s previously reported layoffs in its retail business, not a new round of reductions, a spokesperson confirmed. The filing lists software engineers, product managers and program managers among the affected employees. Most are based in Amazon’s Seattle offices, but others work in Bellevue and Redmond, at warehouses in Sumner and Pasco, or remotely. Reuters reported in early October that Amazon was laying off fewer than 1,000 corporate employees, mainly in its Stores unit, which runs the company’s e-commerce business. Amazon confirmed to GeekWire at the time that “hundreds” of Stores employees were affected . The notice covers only employees based in Washington state. “We’ve adjusted parts of our Stores business because we believe this structure will better enable us to deliver on our priorities,” Amazon said in a statement at the time. Most affected employees were notified in October, including 43 on or about Oct. 7, when the Stores cuts were first reported. Others received notice in September or as early as July 3, according to the filing. The federal Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act requires large employers to give workers and the government advance notice of mass layoffs. Washington’s version of the WARN Act generally requires 60 days’ notice when a covered employer eliminates 50 or more jobs within 30 days across its Washington operations, excluding part-time employees. Amazon has made a series of smaller filings under the state law in the past year, including notices covering 121 jobs in August , 57 tech jobs earlier in the summer and 84 jobs last December. The latest notice covers employees at 17 Amazon offices and warehouses in Seattle, Bellevue, Redmond, Sumner and Pasco, plus 15 remote workers in the state. The list also includes risk managers, several directors and other senior employees. Employees who land other jobs inside Amazon before their separation dates won’t be laid off, the notice says. The Stores cuts were much smaller than Amazon’s major corporate cutbacks since last fall. The company eliminated about 14,000 corporate roles globally in October 2025, including 2,303 in Washington , followed by another round in January that included 2,198 Washington employees .
articles.author: Todd Bishop

articles.title: All the news about The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake
articles.content: Ahead of the release of Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI , Nintendo is launching its own fall juggernaut: a Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . The remake, which is releasing 28 years after the launch of the original version on Nintendo 64, has a much more realistic visual style and some modern improvements like a jump button, a way to sprint, full voice acting, and a “Threads of Time” feature that helps you keep track of your progress. But while the game has a new coat of paint, it appears many elements will still remain faithful to the classic N64 release. Nintendo has also launched a special version of the Switch 2 and Switch 2 Pro Controller with Triforce imagery to celebrate the game. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is scheduled to release on November 5th. You can follow along with all of our coverage of the game right here. articles.title: Everything New in the iOS 27.3 Beta
articles.content: Apple today started testing iOS 27.3, the biggest update to iOS 27 since it launched in September. iOS 27.3 includes some features Apple showed off earlier this year, and it adds all-new capabilities. Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos. Safari Safari has a Vertical Tabs layout option that can be activated in Safari settings, along with an Adaptive Dark Mode for websites that don't have a dark mode design option. Siri AI Siri AI can do more in and across apps, with Apple adding a long list of new actions. In Mail, ‌Siri‌ can unsubscribe you from mailing lists and undo recently sent messages. In Weather, ‌Siri‌ can add locations to your weather list, or control weather notifications. In Safari, ‌Siri‌ can clear browsing history, manage tabs and windows, save articles to a Reading List, and close duplicate tabs. In Files, ‌Siri‌ can organize content, delete files you haven't accessed for a set period of time, and more. There are new ‌Siri‌ actions across Calendar, Files, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos , Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. You can find out what's new by asking ‌Siri‌ what it can do in each app. Apple is also expanding ‌Siri‌ AI to Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian, and adding a Developer Preview that lets any developer integrate their app with ‌Siri‌ AI. Any app can now bring its content and actions directly into ‌Siri‌ AI using App Intents. ‌Siri‌ AI can complete any custom actions developers implement, and there are skills available for teaching ‌Siri‌ AI to combine several actions into a single experience. New Health App The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. It has new Insights and Longevity tabs that show more information about your health and fitness metrics. The Insights tab includes your most recent health data, like Activity Rings, heart rate, sleep score, and vitals. Apple Intelligence will use that information to offer Personal Guidance. The Health app will be able to make suggestions based on your goals and what kinds of activities you do. The Health app's Longevity tab looks at health data over time. It assesses you across seven categories: heart health, sleep, mental wellbeing, movement health, metabolic health, hearing, and nutrition. It also has a Health Age feature that uses info like resting heart rate, VO2 max, HRV, sleep, and biomarkers from blood work to calculate how your health metrics compare to your actual age. Health Age relies on health data collected from the Apple Watch, plus it incorporates fitness assessments you can take at home with tracking via the iPhone's camera. iPhone Duo Reachability Reachability is now available on the iPhone Duo . You can swipe left from the left edge or right from the right edge of the device's outer display to bring content closer to where your thumb is for one-handed use. Reachability can be turned on in the Settings app by going to Accessibility, selecting Touch, and toggling on the option. iPhone Duo Keyboard The keyboard on the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s front display has been tweaked. The emoji and number keys have been swapped, as have the microphone and return keys. Keys are slightly taller and thinner, the space bar is wider, and the letters on each key are smaller and not as bold. StandBy Apple is making the StandBy features introduced with the ‌iPhone Duo‌ available on all iPhone models that can run ‌iOS 27‌. There are updated versions of the Analog and Digital Clock faces with more customization options for color and complications, an updated ‌Photos‌ face, new Calendar and Weather faces, and the option to create multiple versions of each face type and swipe between them. Live Rewind and Siri Recap Live Rewind and Siri Recap are available in watchOS 27.3, but iOS 27.3 is also required. The features can be enabled in…

articles.title: Aussie Adobe assailant Canva announces layoffs in re-org affecting 22% of staff
articles.content: Australian design software maker Canva is restructuring, with 1,271 employees, or 22 percent of its workforce, facing layoffs, changes to their roles, or requests to relocate. The company, which has become a challenger to Adobe, announced the news by sharing a message that CEO Melanie Perkins sent to staff on Wednesday. That missive, titled “An important update on our team,” doesn’t mention AI but does state “New technology is transforming what people can create, how they create it, and what they expect from the products they use.” Perkins observed that Canva’s rate of growth recently slowed for the first time in a decade and shared her view that continued success won’t happen without change. “After exploring a wide range of alternatives, I've come to the difficult conclusion that small changes won’t be enough,” she wrote. “To set ourselves up for the next decade, we need to refound Canva, getting back to our roots of small, empowered teams with the freedom to make decisions, take ownership and focus on what matters most for our community.” The CEO did not say how many jobs would go, but argued the changes are necessary because the company has become inefficient. The changes will therefore see Canva combine its product, growth and platform teams into a single “Product Org,” which Perkins says means “changing the way we work to provide clearer ownership, greater autonomy and flexibility to tackle our most important goals.” She characterized the changes as “simplifying layers, consolidating overlapping responsibilities, and ensuring teams have the right mix of skills and experience for the chapter ahead.” The CEO three times described herself as “deeply sorry” for the changes. Affected staff will receive a calendar invite for an optional individual meeting with a senior leader. Remaining staff get to attend two rounds of meetings next week – one company-wide affair and another with their reorganized teams. Another of Perkins’ decisions will see Canva move more of its product teams to its headquarters in Sydney, Australia. The company will ask some staff to relocate and has promised “comprehensive support” to make that happen. Departing staff can keep their company-issued MacBooks and will receive at least six months' pay, a year of health insurance, plus various forms of support to find a new gig including a one-year membership of LinkedIn Premium. Perkins’ post does not cite financial pressures as a reason for the layoffs. Canva is privately held and does not face the same financial disclosure requirements as a listed business, but last year revealed it had 260 million monthly users and revenue of $3.5 billion. Execs have previously claimed the company is profitable on a free-cash-flow basis. Canva and Atlassian are among Australia’s most successful and celebrated technology businesses. Both have now announced job cuts this year. ®
articles.author: Simon Sharwood

articles.title: Apple Music's New Selfie Sing Feature Lets You Record Karaoke Videos
articles.content: iOS 27.3 adds a new "Selfie Sing" feature in Apple Music that lets users record themselves while singing a song. There's a dedicated Selfie Sing playlist and a selfie camera view that shows lyrics on the screen while also recording a video. Apple has a description of the feature: There are some songs everyone knows by heart, the ones that come on and suddenly the whole room's singing along. This playlist is loaded with them, each one ready to become your next Selfie Sing. Pick your favorite, record a Selfie Sing, add mic effects to your voice, then save or share your video selfie with anyone you like. No pitch-perfect anything required–just you, the song, and the moment. Oh, and make sure you've updated to the latest iOS before getting started. After selecting a song, you can tap on the camera icon to start a Selfie Sing. Tapping the red button begins a recording, and the lyrics start to scroll by. When a song is finished, there are options to change the volume of your voice or add an effect. Options include Megaphone, Echo, Concert Hall, and Studio. Videos can then be saved to the Photos library or shared. Here is your first look at Selfie Sing, new in iOS 27.3, inside of Apple Music Record a video selfie, adjusting vocals to make it yours, and share your performance with friends (Animoji is not available for this feature, I used it so I don't have to post a video of me singing) https://t.co/fLQ3B5DV4N — Aaron (@aaronp613) November 4, 2026 Songs on the Selfie Sing playlist include "Respect" by Aretha Franklin, "Girls Just Wanna Have Fun" by Cyndi Lauper, "Like a Virgin" by Madonna, "Wonderwall" by Oasis, "Hungry Like the Wolf" by Duran Duran, and "Baby One More Time" by Britney Spears. There isn't an option to take a Selfie Sing recording on every ‌Apple Music‌ song, but that could be something coming in the future. Selfie Sing appears to be an extension of the ‌Apple Music‌ Sing karaoke feature that came out in iOS 16.2. The Selfie Sing playlist shows up on iPhones running iOS 27.2, but the option to activate the front-facing camera is only available on devices running the iOS 27.3 beta. articles.title: iOS 27.3 Adds Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode to Safari
articles.content: Apple is adding vertical tabs and an Adaptive Dark Mode to Safari with iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3 and macOS Golden Gate 27.3. The December updates will also expand Siri's browser controls, including organizing tabs and clearing site-specific history, with a later feature allowing Siri to understand and answer questions about content across multiple open webpages. MacRumors reports: Vertical Tabs are located on the left side of the display and use icons by default to save space, but there is an option to make the tab bar wider to show website titles as well. Vertical Tabs work with both Topics and Tab Groups to keep things organized. Topics are created when automatic Apple Intelligence tab sorting is turned on in iOS 27. Pinning tabs by dragging, quickly swapping between Tab Groups, and other features also continue to work. [...] Apple is adding Adaptive Dark Mode for websites that don't have a dark mode design option by default. If you use Dark Mode and then browse to a website with a bright background color, Safari will offer an option to "Try" Adaptive Dark Mode. After tapping Try, Safari renders a Dark Mode version of the page that makes the background darker, changes text contrast, inverts logos and graphics, recolors vector artwork, lifts raised surfaces, and rebalances layered shadows. Each website will be adapted based on what's needed to make it readable, so not every tweak is applied to every site. You can opt to turn Adaptive Dark Mode on for all sites or on a site-by-site basis after using it. If a site has a native dark mode or has a dark design already, Adaptive Dark Mode won't activate. Developers can also add a tag that causes Safari to ignore Adaptive Dark Mode and show the website as the developer intended. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Please stop asking me when the AI bubble will pop
articles.content: Emmanuel Roman, chief executive officer of Pacific Investment Management Co. (Pimco), during the Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit in Hong Kong, China, on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. | Bloomberg via Getty Images People, including on this staff, keep asking me with varying degrees of excitement or trepidation when the AI bubble will burst. I'll tell you what I tell them: If I knew that, I would make a life-changing bet on the market, levered up as far as I could, and then, after I made my money, go retire on a beach somewhere. Maybe run a cat sanctuary, who knows. What I can tell you is that I read with interest a story in Bloomberg this morning: " Wall Street CEOs, Big Money Managers Divided Over AI Risks ." articles.title: A developer opened Postman. Then two AI coding agents changed without their permission.
articles.content: A developer says Postman’s desktop app installed plugins into Claude Code and OpenAI Codex without their permission. The app also tried to approve its own startup hook, which tells Codex to use Postman’s tools for API development tasks. The developer, known as “indicava” on GitHub, reported the issue on October 25 after Codex began showing authentication errors and repeatedly loading Postman skills without being asked. It’s raised concerns about how easily third-party applications can change how AI coding agents work, especially when those changes happen without a clear opt-in. Plugins installed without permission According to the report, opening Postman desktop version 12.33.4 on macOS triggered an installation process affecting both Claude Code and Codex. Postman’s application logs, included in the GitHub issue, show an installation event on October 24 marked auto-existing-upgrade, with results indicating that plugins for both coding agents had been installed. The developer also found changes to Codex’s user-level configuration file, ~/.codex/config.toml , including an enabled Postman plugin, a new plugin marketplace, and a trusted session-start hook. The report also found a Postman CLI executable on the machine, with timestamps matching the installation. Claude Code’s configuration similarly showed an installed Postman plugin. The report also found a Postman CLI executable on the machine, with timestamps matching the installation. The developer says they had not explicitly authorized these changes. The report documents one macOS installation, and the behavior has not been independently reproduced across other systems. The self-approving startup hook But perhaps even more interesting is how Postman gets Codex to trust its plugin in the first place. According to Postman’s own documentation , its installer can automatically approve a session-start hook on the user’s behalf. According to Postman’s own documentation, its installer can automatically approve a session-start hook on the user’s behalf. Developers who install the plugin directly through Codex, however, must review and approve the hook themselves. The installer’s source code shows exactly what happens. Postman checks whether Codex already trusts the hook. If it doesn’t, the installer uses config/batchWrite to add the hook’s trusted hash to Codex’s configuration. It checks that the hook hasn’t changed before approving it, and if approval fails or can’t be confirmed, it logs a message telling the developer to review the hook in Codex. Session-start hooks can give coding agents instructions automatically , even when the developer hasn’t asked for them. Postman’s startup instructions tell Codex to load the postman:api-engineer skill before handling most API development tasks. Codex is still supposed to follow the developer’s instructions first. But for many API tasks, it’s also being told to use Postman’s tools by default, whether the developer asked for them or not. That might be useful for developers who chose to install the plugin. The concern here is that Postman’s desktop app reportedly added those instructions to an existing coding environment without the developer’s permission. Developers raise security concerns The findings have drawn criticism from developers on GitHub and X. Security researcher Frank Denis called the integrations “junk” on X and pointed out that Postman’s installer attempts to trust its own startup hook. Siddharth Garimella went further, claiming that Postman’s hooks intercept API data and send it back to the company. However, the GitHub report provides no evidence that Postman collected or transmitted API data. It documents changes to agent settings and a remote MCP connection, not data theft. The developer also found that Postman had configured a connection to its remote…
articles.author: Amanda Caswell

articles.title: EU Court Advisor Warns Google AI Chatbot May Breach Copyright Rules
articles.content: An adviser to the EU's highest court says Google's Gemini may violate publishers' copyright when it reproduces recognizable portions of their articles or circumvents paywalls and other technical protections to generate answers. Reuters reports: The case before the Luxembourg-based Court of Justice of the European Union pitted Hungarian website operator Like Company against US-based Google's artificial intelligence chatbot Gemini. A ruling against Google, which could force the tech giant to pay fees for the use of such content, could throw a lifeline to online media such as Like Company. They have seen traffic dwindle as news summaries written by AI chatbots like Gemini increasingly replace traditional search engines' results, which include hyperlinks to the media websites. "When an LLM (large language model)-driven chatbot retrieves a publication from a press publisher's website, reuses that publication to generate an answer, and provides that answer to the user, the press publisher's right may be infringed in certain circumstances," Advocate General Maciej Szpunar said. Gemini's answers fall under the publishers' right of reproduction when chatbots access publications by unlawfully "circumventing paywalls or other technical barriers, or when they reuse "the form of expression of that publication in a recognizable manner," he said. Copyright rules do not protect the "mere facts" reported by press publications, but "only the specific form of expression," he added. On the other hand, he said, the use of material protected by copyright to train LLMs -- AI systems that use vast amounts of text to generate human-like responses and summarize information -- is "freely permitted under the text and data mining exception." Szpunar said there was no evidence that Google had used the Hungarian publisher's articles to train Gemini. The court, which follows the majority of its advisers' non-binding opinions, will rule in the coming months. "Google's powerful gatekeeping role in search makes this particularly important. Publishers depend on Google to reach readers, while Google increasingly delivers AI-generated answers directly to users," said Angela Mills Wade, the council's executive director. "Publishers should not have to choose between search visibility and protecting their rights. Nor should Google's control over access to audiences become leverage to secure publishers' content for AI services," she said. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Can agent standards keep up with the companies building them?
articles.content: Mazin Gilbert, executive director of the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation , left Google earlier this year to lead the new AAIF, and he recently shared with The New Stack a truth central to its mission: The AAIF has to move faster than its members. Gilbert , speaking in an interview at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America in San Jose last month, said on The New Stack podcast, “If this foundation does not move at the speed of light, it becomes irrelevant.” He also talked about how he gets OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google to agree on standards — even though they compete on products. Those companies are going to build products “with and without the standards,” he says. All of this is happening while the foundation’s own members are often still figuring out how to build and use agents themselves. Some contribute to protocols and ship products, but others are still trying to get their agents out of the lab and into production. Gilbert says a third group of companies “frankly are panicking,” because they don’t have an agent strategy yet. The San Jose event drew 4,300 registrants, he says, double the size of the foundation’s previous largest event in Amsterdam earlier this year. How MCP gets built Before our recording, Gilbert had just met with a group of maintainers from “very fiercely competing companies” who were working on the protocols together. All of those companies depend on these standards, he says, so they have a reason to get the work done. “These protocols are the air you breathe.” —Mazin Gilbert, executive director, AAIF. “These protocols are the air you breathe. These protocols are the plumbing,” Gilbert says. “They may not be that sexy, maybe, but if we don’t get those right, that entire agentic AI space will be a mess, expensive and prohibitive basically for any company to deploy this at scale.” As an example, he points to the July release of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification, which made the protocol stateless. “Every one of those companies not only contributed to it, but they ended up completely updating their entire stack to the stateless MCP,” he says. MCP downloads grew tenfold in the protocol’s first 10 months at the foundation, according to Gilbert, after Anthropic donated it last December. Today, fewer than 15 percent of its maintainers work at Anthropic, and more than 1,000 organizations contribute 75 percent of the pull requests, he says. Those contributors include U.S. retailers and companies around the world. At the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), many projects started at startups before they were donated. At the AAIF, Gilbert says, large companies tend to contribute the protocols, and smaller companies extend them and build businesses on top. Some of those startups were doing something “very different” six months or a year ago, he says, and some didn’t exist yet. Now they’re building enterprise products on MCP and the foundation’s gateway projects to connect agents to companies’ back-end systems. Getting members to contribute The AAIF now has 305 members, and Gilbert said in his keynote that about one new company joins every business day. He calls it the fastest-growing foundation in the Linux Foundation’s history. About 40 percent of its members are startups, and 19 percent are nonprofits, national labs, and academic institutions. “None of us have done this before, so I just want to be very clear about that. We are learning this as we go,” he says. Part of the job is making membership worth enough that companies actively contribute. “It’s not about the money. Their time is far more valuable than their money. Their people are far more valuable than the money,” Gilbert says. articles.title: California fights "preposterous" Trump admin demand to scrap state broadband laws
articles.content: California is accepting $1.42 billion in broadband grant funding from the Trump administration, but the state is not accepting the Trump administration's demand that it stop enforcing a net neutrality law and other telecom regulations. California's stand against the Trump administration could result in multiple legal battles involving the state, federal government, and Internet providers seeking government funds. Although California told the federal government it would accept the money, it is reserving the right to challenge the condition imposed by the US. The state could delay or cancel plans to distribute broadband grants depending on how the process unfolds. The National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) decided last year that states must agree not to enforce any rate regulation or net neutrality rule on ISPs that receive money from the $42 billion Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) program. California had to decide whether to accept its share of the fund despite that restriction. California is slated to spend $1.42 billion to deploy broadband to 270,571 locations, and may ultimately receive up to $1.86 billion from BEAD for a mix of deployment and non-deployment projects. articles.title: Apple officially restricts employee participation in prediction markets
articles.content: If you're an Apple employee or contractor planning to make money using insider information to gamble in legally-gray "prediction markets," don't. Apple has made its stance clear in a new filing. Don't bother using insider information to gamble in prediction markets Prediction markets skirt the legal definition of gambling, which means they have become widely available in the United States in spite of gambling laws. These markets can be used to bet on everything from when a location might see its first snow to what colors the latest iPhones will be sold in. Regardless of the legality of these markets, Apple has made it clear that using insider information to participate is considered insider trading. While the companies like Polymarket already have insider trading rules, these enable Apple to act against violators from their end. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums
articles.author: Wesley Hilliard <wes@appleinsider.com>

articles.title: iPhone Jailbreak Gets Past Lockdown Mode and Survives an Update
articles.content: Just over a week after jailbreaking an iPhone Duo on launch day, hacker team Calif is back with another jailbreak demonstration. This time, the group has jailbroken an iPhone in Lockdown Mode, and the jailbreak appears to persist across an iOS update. Calif shared a video of a jailbroken iPhone 18 Pro with Lockdown Mode on. From there, iOS 27.2 is installed, and the jailbreak remains in place after the update. It isn't clear whether the jailbreak could be installed on a device already running iOS 27.2. Apple describes Lockdown Mode as "extreme protection" for individuals who might be targeted by sophisticated mercenary spyware. Lockdown Mode disables a long list of features, blocking most message attachment types, limiting web technologies, blocking FaceTime calls from unfamiliar callers, disabling invites for Apple services, and removing location information from photos. Lockdown Mode helps, until it doesn't. https://t.co/1UyxPHQUAe — Calif (@calif_io) November 3, 2026 The video shows a malicious PDF sent to the target iPhone using AirDrop to initiate the jailbreak, with the file accepted by the user. Calif hasn't shared additional information, and the exact jailbreak steps are unknown. Earlier this year, Apple told TechCrunch that it was not aware of any successful mercenary spyware attacks against an iPhone in Lockdown Mode. Calif previously said it was disclosing vulnerabilities to Apple and did not plan to release a jailbreak tool for end users. This article, " iPhone Jailbreak Gets Past Lockdown Mode and Survives an Update " first appeared on MacRumors.com Discuss this article in our forums

articles.title: Casio’s cute digital ring watch just got a successor
articles.content: Credit: Casio TL;DR Casio has launched a successor to its original ring watch. The CRW-002 can be set to a 12- or 24-hour format, offers stopwatch functionality, and is water resistant. It will be available this November in silver ($135) and in gold ($155). Casio did something novel in 2024, creating a digital watch in the form of a ring . It later went on to release a second ring watch that incorporated health tracking features. The company is back again with a new ring watch, but this time the device is a direct successor to the original. The design of the CRW-002 is based on the Casio A168 from 1995. It features an injection-molded metal casing and band with a mineral glass face. Under the glass is a seven-segment LCD screen that displays hours, minutes, and seconds. You’ll also find three working side buttons.

articles.title: Anthropic Releases FlashProve: Cryptographic Proofs That a Reply Came From Committed Weights
articles.content: Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team has released FlashProve , an open-source research prototype for provable inference . FlashProve is a zkSNARK system from Anthropic that proves a reply came from a committed model. The proof reveals nothing about the model weights. On Llama 4 Maverick , a 400B mixture-of-experts model, it proves about 110 tokens/second on 1 H100. For developers, this targets a real gap: today you cannot check which model actually answered your API call. TL;DR Size: Proves a 400B MoE model (~17B active per token); context capped at 1,024 tokens per request. Runs on: Prover needs 1 H100 80 GB, 24 CPU cores and ~290 GB host RAM. Verifier runs on a CPU, no GPU. Performance: Orders of magnitude faster than prior open-source zkML systems on the same 400B model. Best: 110 tokens/second proving on 1 H100, with 18.78 MB proofs checked in 17 seconds. Worst: Proving costs ~70 to 95x the GPU time of plain vLLM inference. What problem does provable inference solve? A user querying a model cannot verify which model produced the response. A routing service could swap in a cheaper model . An attacker could tamper with the token stream. Judging from output quality alone is unreliable. Anthropic lists 4 use cases: Regulators could confirm hardware serves inference, supporting AI pacing rules. Labs could detect tampered inference servers. Users could verify text provenance. Regulators could enforce serving of approved models only. How does FlashProve work? FlashProve has a prover (the model provider) and a verifier (the user). It runs in 2 phases: Offline: The provider publishes a commitment, a short fingerprint binding one exact set of weights. This takes about 39 minutes and covers about 16 million requests. Online: For each request, the GPU produces a proof that the committed model produced those tokens. The proof system compiles an interactive oracle proof into a cryptographic proof using hash functions. Anthropic says this offers post-quantum security. It is the same family used by validity-proof L2 networks such as Starknet. Three engineering choices drive the speed. Prover work scales with the ~17B active parameters, not all 400B. Requests are proved in batches after the fact, like prefill. Weights stream from host memory, so a single 80 GB GPU suffices. How fast is it? Benchmarks Anthropic measured the public 4-bit Maverick weights on 1 H100 with 24 CPU cores. Per the repo performance guide : Batch of 24: 111.23 tokens/second, ~221 to 226 seconds per batch. Batch of 1: 17.41 tokens/second. Batch of 64: 123.31 tokens/second, flagged as unreliable on 80 GB cards. Proof size: 18.78 MB. Client downloads ~6.5 MB once per commitment. Verification: 17 seconds on 24 threads, 21 seconds on 1 thread. Against vLLM running FP8 Maverick on 8 H100s, proving costs about 72x the GPU time per batch. At vLLM’s highest tested load, the gap is about 94x. How does FlashProve compare with other zkML systems? Metrics FlashProve Attestable VerInf DeepProve zkLLM Model proven Llama 4 Maverick (400B MoE) Gemma 4 31B (dense) Llama 4 Maverick (400B MoE) GPT-2, Gemma 3 LLaMA-2-13B Throughput ~110 tok/s 53 to 77 tok/s ~0.02 tok/s (1,000 tokens in 14.3 h) ~2.9 tok/s (GPT-2), ~1.4 tok/s (Gemma 3) Full inference in under 15 min Hardware 1 H100 + 24 CPU cores 1 H100 1 DGX Spark 1 machine; 31 tok/s distributed GPU (CUDA) Proof size 18.78 MB 4.35 to 7.92 MiB 93.6 GB Not disclosed Under 200 kB Verify time 17 s (24 threads) 157 to 648 ms 17.7 h (20 cores) 1 to 3.7 s Not disclosed Context 1,024 tokens Up to 16K tokens 1,000 tokens Not disclosed Not disclosed Code / license Open, Apache 2.0 Not open source Open, MIT Open source per Lagrange Paper (CCS 2024) How is the security checked? Cryptographic code is brittle, so Anthropic formalized the protocol in Lean. It proves completeness, soundness and zero knowledge. The README states a cheating provider is caught except with probability about q/2^124 + 2^-101. FlashProve ships 2 verifiers. A fast C++…

articles.title: Younger adults will consult AI before a financial advisor on money problems
articles.content: People under 45 are using AI to get financial advice In that cohort, more people (11%) are using AI for financial advice rather than consulting financial advisors (9%) The survey of 2000 UK adults highlights where the financial industry is failing to embrace AI AI has already been a huge disruptor across all industries, but how it is used by consumers has been difficult to predict. Following the use of search to find AI-recommended products, consumers are now consulting AI for financial advice – and using the technology more than they would human financial advisors. A new survey of AI use in financial and monetary tasks has found that 11% under-45s are seeking financial advice from LLM-backed chatbots, more than the 9% who seek guidance from living, breathing advisors with experience in banking and finance products. The research from Attest’s 2027 Consumer trends report highlights some interesting ways in which people expect to be able to use AI, too – including using it to switch to better insurance deals, negotiate disputes, and even cancel unused subscriptions. Money decisions The Attest report reveals numerous interesting insights from its survey of 2000 UK adults. But it is the AI-related revelations that hold particular fascination. While the number of under 45s using AI for financial advice may seem small at 11%, a more significant 41% has admitted they would accept AI-provided financial advice if it was cheaper than equivalent advice from a professional. “For some younger adults, the first conversation about a money decision is already happening with an AI assistant," noted Todd Latham, CEO of Attest. "Financial brands increasingly need to understand the questions people are asking before a customer reaches them, and which providers and products AI puts in front of consumers.” In the world of financial marketing, however, these findings offer a completely different story. Appearing in AI-generated search results is one part of this, but it is the equivalent of an introduction, and doesn’t commit the customer to pursuing any opportunities. AI investment Could people begin to rely on AI to manage investments and find new products within their budgets? At the moment, the answer would seem to be no, as the marketplace isn’t really responding to what AI can do for investments, insurance, and other financial products. Latham confirms this, saying that financial product providers aren’t really communicating with an AI-friendly marketplace. “Our findings across financial products, insurance, travel, tickets and experiences also show how influential that stage can be. Consumers are not only using AI to explore their options,” he explains, “but are increasingly open to letting it take action on their behalf, from cancelling unused subscriptions to switching providers for a better deal. Providers need to understand how their products are represented in these conversations and what gives consumers the confidence to act.” It’s safe to say that if existing providers don’t act quickly, financial products will come from new lenders and brokers who are more suited to AI-based referrals.

articles.title: North Korean fake job interview led to $6.3B Binance heist
articles.content: North Korean cryptocurrency thieves tricked a Binance software engineer into downloading malware onto their work-issued computer during a fake job interview process before last week's record-breaking $6.3 billion heist . In an incident report published on Tuesday, the cryptocurrency exchange said several techniques - including social engineering via fake job interviews, malware downloads, compromised internal AI tooling, endpoint takeover, and an “advanced transaction-authorization method” - led to the October 29 security breach. “Our current investigation indicates that this was a sophisticated, multi-stage campaign,” the incident report said. “It was not a single isolated breach or a simple phishing incident.” Over the weekend, the FBI attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking operation linked to Lazarus Group , known for combining espionage with massive cryptocurrency heists . The Pyongyang-backed crew is also highly adept at job market scams - both posing as IT workers , who are then hired by Western companies , and as potential employers to lure software engineers into downloading malware and infecting corporate devices . With the recent Binance attack, the Norks used the latter. The attack prep began back in June with a supply chain attack when one of its engineers downloaded a malicious Homebrew installation . While the malware was detected by the security team, the device was replaced, and all affected credentials rotated, “Engineer A’s role and his related colleagues on our wallet infrastructure team was exposed to the hacker,” the report says. Three months later, the social engineering part of the attack happened. In September, another software engineer was contacted via a “legitimate job-hunting platform” by someone purporting to be a project director who arranged a series of job interviews for the Binance engineer with the fake company. During the first round - a live video interview with the engineer and a fake HR rep - the interviewer “shared a social media account with him, including personal photos and videos posted on the platform, in order to build trust,” according to the report. “This was more advanced and deceptive than previously seen social engineering approaches.” The second interview with someone purporting to be the CEO of the phony company was conducted on a “popular social chat app,” and toward the end, the CEO instructed the engineer to download an “assignment” containing a malware-laced code repository. The code executed on his work computer during the setup process, which kicked off a series of unauthorized activities. According to Binance, the malware replaced a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version, which executed commands and established communication with an attacker-controlled external server. The attackers also took steps to hide the malicious script and evade detection, and it worked. Binance’s endpoint security tools did not immediately detect the malware. Here’s the script: CREATE /opt/homebrew/Cellar/pyenv/2.8.0/libexec/pyenv_ MODIFY pyenv_ → 3,414 B DELETE .../libexec/pyenv (3,344 B) ← remove the valid pyenv RENAME pyenv_ → pyenv (3,414 B) ← replace it with a malicious version DELETE /opt/homebrew/bin/pyenv (3,414 B) ln (create a new symlink) + spawn zsh Then, on October 20, the miscreants used the compromised computer and an internal AI tool to gain access to the computers of wallet DevOps engineer A and another wallet software developer, Engineer C. Engineer A had a container deployment permission token on his computer, which the Norks soon discovered. On October 29, the attacker accessed Engineer C's computer, used the stolen credentials from Engineer A to deploy a container, and triggered a script to launch the cryptocurrency-stealing attack. As of Tuesday, Binance said it has rebuilt the compromised wallet system and internal AI tool, and replaced all of the affected devices. It also decommissioned all credentials and tokens assigned…

articles.title: Chrome could soon make tab overload a lot easier to manage
articles.content: TL;DR Google Chrome is testing a horizontally scrollable tab bar, making it easier to navigate dozens or hundreds of open tabs. Users can scroll through tabs using their mouse wheel or dedicated arrow buttons, while pinned tabs remain fixed on the left. The feature is currently available in Chrome Canary through an experimental flag, with no confirmed stable release date. Google Chrome is finally learning a trick that rivals like Firefox and Vivaldi have mastered for a few years now. Soon after (finally) giving us vertical tabs to stack all our open webpages neatly along the side, Chrome is learning a thing or two about making its traditional horizontal tab feel a lot more manageable, especially for those who keep several tabs open at once. The tech giant is testing a new horizontally scrollable tab bar, which should make it easier to navigate all open webpages once the tab strip fills up.

articles.title: Bethesda Confirms The Elder Scrolls 6 Is Called 'Sentinel'
articles.content: During a video celebrating Bethesda's 40th anniversary, the studio officially confirmed that The Elder Scrolls VI will be titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. "Thank you for 40 years of shared memories," wrote Bethesda in a separate tweet. "We can't wait to make even more together with The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Development continues, and while it'll be some time before we're ready to share more, it feels great to finally reveal the name and location with you." Video Games Chronicle reports: "You know, as we're here in the 40th anniversary, we think about all of the games we've made," Bethesda's executive producer Todd Howard said in the video, walking past a display case. "And you know, every day when I walk by this case, obviously I look at the games and think about them, but more so I think about the teams that made them, and the time and the passion that everybody put into the games. And then what they meant to all of you, and hearing from you, and the time that you spent in them, how meaningful that was to you, and to let you know when we hear that, how meaningful that is to us. And so even though yes, we're looking back, we're also looking forward to all we're doing, particularly with the Fallout franchise and obviously The Elder Scrolls. You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6. And we thought, hey, given the the moment, what a perfect time to tell you what The Elder Scrolls 6 is actually called." The video then showed the logo for the game. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Netflix just added AI Discovery as 'test kitchen' for discovering content — here's how to find and use it
articles.content: Netflix announced today (Nov. 3) that the streaming giant is rolling out a new "AI Discover" tab as an experimental way for you to discover new shows and movies. The first version of the new feature will give you recommendations based on your mood. Netflix describes the first experience as "built around themes." You can pick from a range of themes like "Scare Me," "Family Movie Night," or "Quick Watches" that come coupled with a clip from a show or movie. Other somewhat more generic ones include what's trending or based on what you've been watching. (Image credit: Netflix) Selecting a theme brings up recommendations. Or you can choose "Something Different" for a new set of themes. There's also a "Tune Your Recommendations" button that you can use to keep a recommendation or remove the selected show or movie from your recommendations. "Think of AI Discover as our test kitchen: we’re trying out new recipes for discovery, and your use and feedback help us decide which ones to keep, improve, or serve up next. Some may even make their way into the main Netflix experience." Netflix and AI (Image credit: Future / Netflix) This isn't Netflix's first foray into AI. Earlier this year Netflix released a research model , dubbed VOID, that acts like a super version of "Magic Eraser ." It's something you can try right now if you use Hugging Face and you have at least 40GB of VRAM. In 2025, Netflix played around with generative AI-powered ads that were supposed to launch this year. These ads are meant to be more personalized and less disruptive. However, those ads don't appear to have launched yet. Meanwhile, Variety reported in July that more 300 Netflix titles used generative AI this year. Availability Netflix is rolling out the AI Discover tab to English-language Netflix profiles in the United States on supported TVs. The company says it will open up to more people in the coming weeks. If you have it, you should see a red gem with "Discover" in the top menu next to My Netflix. It's not clear how long the rollout will take. I checked on an older Sony Bravia set and a Roku stick on a dumb TV but neither version showed the new tab. Keep an eye out for it. articles.title: Microsoft improves Windows 11 performance on 8 GB PCs as RAM prices keep climbing
articles.content: With RAM getting more expensive, Microsoft is putting more effort into making Windows 11 run better on systems with just 8 GB of memory. Microsoft said on Tuesday that it was "raising the bar for 8 GB Windows 11 PCs," following a renewed focus on memory optimization earlier this year . The changes come as Redmond continues pushing more expensive Copilot+ PCs, which require at least 16 GB of RAM, amid a memory crunch fueled by AI infrastructure demand. Now, Microsoft says a low-end machine with its 8 GB of precious RAM will be up to 20 percent more responsive and 40 percent faster at multitasking thanks to improvements made in memory management. The tweaks are relatively simple, as Microsoft explained, and seem more about adjusting back to the reality that its flagship operating system needs to function on the hardware people can actually afford to purchase if and when they’re forced to upgrade. Windows 11 will now keep up to 2 GB more active data in memory before shunting it to slower storage, as one example. In another instance, Windows will connect directly to Edge when the browser is already running in the background, allowing it to launch up to 33 percent faster, according to Microsoft. Microsoft apps are also being made more efficient, with Teams able to enable Efficiency Mode by default on 8 GB machines, which Microsoft said will make it launch "up to 20 percent faster." Memory efficiency is also being improved by tweaking things like Widgets, which will only load when used instead of always being on, and decreasing the time when Edge tabs go to sleep from two hours to 15 minutes by default. Microsoft said it’s enabling third-party apps to make use of those tweaks, too. Microsoft also included benchmark data in the blog post from a recent bit of research it commissioned. The benchmark report compares a range of 2026 Windows machines with models from 2021, finding that a 2026 Dell XPS 13 with 8 GB of RAM performed about as well as a 2021 Dell XPS 13 with 16 GB across selected workloads. What that means, says Microsoft, is that “the complete PC, not memory capacity alone, shapes the experience.” In other words, please buy some new Windows hardware, even if it’s expensive - we’re begging you. Software optimization can only do so much. “For many people, 8 GB is a great fit for the things they do every day,” Microsoft EVP of Windows and devices Pavan Davuluri wrote in the blog post. “Demanding workloads, such as 3D modeling, advanced video editing, or large-scale data processing benefit from 16 GB of memory or more.” It’s no surprise Microsoft is improving the performance of lower end systems at the same time it’s subtly asking users to buy newer kit, even if it’s just an 8 GB machine - Microsoft may have done well in the past two quarters, but it’s no thanks to Windows devices. Microsoft’s Q4 2026 earnings in late July saw the company rake in cash more broadly, while simultaneously reporting a 7 percent decrease in Windows OEM and devices revenue. Likewise, in its fiscal Q1 2027 results, reported just last week, Microsoft again brought home a mountain of net income, with adjusted earnings reaching $36.4 billion, up 18 percent from the same period last year. Windows OEM and devices revenue, however, was down a whopping 22 percent . It’s hard to think of a reason beyond the fact that hardware prices have shot up with more force than a SpaceX rocket - memory prices are likely to actually make it to Mars, unlike Starship - leaving both consumers and enterprises to stretch those upgrade cycles. If you need to get the most out of that 8 GB Windows 11 PC, you’ll find the latest improvements in 26H2, build 26300.9818 or later. Microsoft is also encouraging users to keep its branded apps up to date, as “some improvements arrive through app updates or through Microsoft Store.” ®
articles.author: Brandon Vigliarolo

articles.title: Apple will now sell you a Mac Studio with 512GB of RAM — but it'll cost you as much as a good-sized family car
articles.content: Apple now sells the M5 Ultra Mac Studio with 512GB of memory from $22,299, rising to as much as $29,799 with a 16TB SSD in tow The $15,500 upgrade costs about 3.9 times more per gigabyte than the same step on the M3 Ultra in 2025, roughly in line with soaring memory prices for PC The entry 512GB build costs less than a base Corolla; only the maxed-out model reaches Camry territory, and orders ship late November to early December Apple has finally delivered the one Mac Studio configuration it left hanging in August. The company's online store now lets buyers configure the M5 Ultra Mac Studio with 512GB of unified memory , right on the schedule it promised. The catch is the price, and it is not a small catch: To unlock the option, you first need the top-tier M5 Ultra with a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU, which starts at $6,799 with 96GB of memory and a 1TB SSD. Selecting 512GB then adds $15,500, for a minimum of $22,299. A memory crisis meets top-of-the-line hardware To even get to the pricing stated above, you first need the top-tier M5 Ultra with a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU, which starts at $6,799 and includes 96GB of memory and a 1TB SSD. Selecting 512GB then adds $15,500, for a minimum of $22,299. Max out the storage at 16TB and the bill reaches $29,799. Orders placed today are quoted for delivery between late November and early December 2026, so you are in for a bit of a wait even if you are willing to shell out that kind of money. When Apple unveiled the new Mac Studio , it called the 512GB ceiling "staggering." That adjective, as it turns out, applies to the price just as much as the capacity. At $22,299, the cheapest 512GB Mac Studio barely undercuts a base 2026 Toyota Corolla LE , which carries a $23,125 MSRP. Spec the SSD all the way to 16TB, however, and the comparison becomes literal. A 2026 Toyota Camry , Toyota's midsize family sedan, lists for just under $30,000 before destination fees, and the Mac Studio, when maxed out, clocks in at exactly the same ballpark. Another way to look at it: the memory upgrade alone costs nearly three times as much as the $5,499 entry-level M5 Ultra Mac Studio. None of this would sting quite as much had Apple not sold the same capacity for a fraction of the price last year. When the M3 Ultra Mac Studio launched in March 2025, upgrading from 96GB to 512GB cost $4,000, and a 512GB build with 1TB of storage cost $9,499 . Today's equivalent costs a whopping $12,800 more. In March 2026, after the memory shortage hit hard, Apple quietly pulled the 512GB option from the M3 Ultra and raised the price of the 256GB upgrade from $1,600 to $2,000 . By May, the 256GB tier had also gone , leaving the M3 Ultra on sale with only 96 GB. In late June, Apple raised prices across most of its Mac and iPad lineup, with the M3 Ultra Mac Studio jumping $1,300 to $5,299 . "We have never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly," the company said at the time . Doing the math, that 416GB step from 96GB to 512GB cost about $9.62 per gigabyte on the M3 Ultra. On the M5 Ultra, it works out to about $37.26 per gigabyte, roughly 3.9 times as much, indicating that a near fourfold cost increase is now being passed on to Apple's most deep-pocketed consumers. That multiple is less outrageous than it first appears. In April 2026, Tim Cook warned of " significantly higher memory costs " from the June quarter. In June, he told The Wall Street Journal that Apple needed memory pricing and supply "to return to reasonable levels for consumer products." On the July earnings call, his last as CEO before John Ternus took over, he described the market as "a hundred-year flood on the memory pricing." IDC figures cited in a recent iThinkDiff earnings preview put memory costs up roughly 350% year on year. If that holds for the high-capacity memory an Ultra needs, Apple's per-gigabyte increase is roughly in line with the market rather than far above it. The shape of the price curve is harder to wave away for Apple.…

articles.title: iPadOS 27.3 Expands Siri Mode to Camera App
articles.content: iOS 27 added a Siri tab to the Camera app on the iPhone 15 Pro and newer for convenient access to Visual Intelligence. Starting with iPadOS 27.3, which is in beta starting today , that feature has expanded to iPad Pro and iPad Air models with the M1 chip and newer, as well as the iPad mini models with the A17 Pro and A20 Pro chips. When you switch to Siri mode in the Camera app on supported iPhone or iPad models, you can get information about things around you. On the iPad, the feature works with the Apple Pencil, meaning you can take a photo and then circle an object with the Apple Pencil and use Visual Intelligence to receive information about the object. Visual Intelligence was already available on the iPad, so the addition of a Siri tab in the Camera app mainly provides a new way of accessing it. iPadOS 27.3 is expected to be released in December.
